newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ broker silent on sudden departure - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: NZ broker silent on sudden departure - newspaper.

text.p: Sharebroker Merrill Lynch is tight-lipped about the recent departure of one of its senior brokers, Wellington's Evening Post newspaper reported on Monday.
Broker Ian Waddell, who was also a director of Merrill Lynch (New Zealand), said his employment contract prevented him from explaining his sudden departure.
It is understood he has been paid up to August 24.
Waddell said he expected to continue working in the sharebroking industry. He would not say whether he had accepted a position with a rival broker.
Merrill Lynch spokesman Matthew Rose said his company would not comment.
Waddell was known to have a number of top international clients.
Meanwhile, fellow broker Garlick and Co has shed its team involved with its fixed interest deals, but made an arrangement for the two staff involved to join Ord Minnett.
Earlier this year Garlick and Co cut 16 jobs from its 27 staff.
Garlick and Co managing director Bill Garlick said the restructuring had worked for his company.
"We are the only independently owned institutional broker. We're 100 percent owned by our staff and we've had three big restructures in 12 years," he told the paper.
"While it always is traumatic to see people leave, it's better a few go rather than the whole lot."
Garlick said by the year 2000 he expected the number of brokers and staff in fund management to be down to a quarter of what it was now.
